title: Right Side View
statement:
List the values you would see looking at a binary tree from its right-hand side.

Contract
- `root` may be null. Each node has an integer `value` and nullable `left` and `right` children.
- Return one value per level, from the root level downward: the value of the rightmost node on that level.
- A node on the left still counts when no node to its right exists on the same level.
- An empty tree gives an empty list. Do not modify the tree.

Examples
- `[5, 2, 8, null, 4, null, 6]` gives `[5, 8, 6]`.
- A null tree gives `[]`.
- `[7, 8, null, 9]` leans left but every level has one node, so the answer is `[7, 8, 9]`.
hints: Group nodes by their distance from the root; each group contributes exactly one value.
Process the tree level by level and remember the last node you meet on each level, or walk right-first and record the first node reached at each new depth.

Visit every node once. Intended complexity: O(n) time for n nodes. A level-order queue holds up to one full level, so extra space is O(n) in the worst case (a right-first depth-first walk needs only O(h) stack plus the result).
inputSyntax: Input: the tree in level order with null for missing children, for example: [5, 2, 8, null, 4, null, 6]
